kernel.governing_law: Love is experienced as pure devastation — an external force that shatters, tramples, corrodes, and etches, leaving the lover destroyed yet radiant in ruin; relation is suffered, never mutual, never covenantal.
kernel.mutated_relation: The devastation as consummation — the force that shatters is the force that joins; what was endured alone becomes what is entered together; ruin becomes threshold.

independent.recovered_law: TEXT A portrays Eros/love as a destructive, solitary force that shatters the self and inflicts pain (wind destroying oaks, trampled flowers, corrosive demons, hurt, pain). TEXT B transforms this into a constructive, mutual, domestic bond that builds and joins (vow founding a household, bread shared, binding covenant, marriage, joy flowing between partners).
independent.law_match_note: Both describe the same structural transformation: destructive/solitary force recast as constructive/mutual joining — shattering becomes threshold, endured alone becomes entered together, ruin becomes union.
independent.terminal_note: The final lines maintain the changed relation: 'your joy / lit face shines / into me' sustains the constructive, mutual direction rather than reverting to TEXT A's pain and reflective separation.
